new_statements.quote: En karone, le ton n’a pas été attesté. Toutefois, la hauteur musicale et l’accent dynamique sont prévisibles dans le mot phonologique, selon les règles suivantes. […] La hauteur musicale est marquée par un ton plus haut sur la syllabe pénultième. […] a) Si le mot contient un ou plusieurs syllabes lourdes, c’est-à-dire du type (C)VV, (C)VVC ou CVNC, celles-ci portent l’accent dynamique. […] b) Une syllabe fermée, c’est-à-dire du type (C)VC, porte l’accent s’il n’y a pas de syllabe lourde pour le porter. […] c) Si toutes les syllabes sont légères, c’est-à-dire du type (C)V, la première syllabe porte l’accent dynamique.
new_statements.translation: In Karone, tone has not been attested. However, musical pitch and dynamic accent are predictable within the phonological word, according to the following rules. [...] Musical pitch is marked by a higher tone on the penultimate syllable. [...] a) If the word contains one or more heavy syllables, i.e. of the type (C)VV, (C)VVC or CVNC, these carry the dynamic accent. [...] b) A closed syllable, i.e. of the type (C)VC, carries the accent if there is no heavy syllable to carry it. [...] c) If all syllables are light, i.e. of the type (C)V, the first syllable carries the dynamic accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No lexical tone. Two predictable word-level prominences are described separately: (i) a pitch peak ('hauteur musicale') always on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word (schemas given for 2-, 3-, 4-syllable words); (ii) intensity stress ('accent dynamique') assigned by syllable weight: every heavy syllable ((C)VV, (C)VVC, CVNC, i.e. long vowel or V+NC coda) is stressed; if there is none, a closed (C)VC syllable is stressed; if all syllables are light (C)V, the first syllable is stressed. Examples: [ˈkɐːwɐk] 'creuser', [ɐˈɲɪː] 'enfant', [cikiˈsoːl] 'laboure!', [ɛlɐˈwʊt], [ˈcɐpɐ] 'oignon', [ˈɛjɐnʊ] 'étang'. I read the stress ('accent dynamique') system as weight-sensitive with default-initial; note the co-existing fixed penultimate pitch peak, which another analyst might take as the 'accent' (hence some risk of an 'unclear' classification).
new_statements.secondary_stress: No primary/secondary ranking: 'un mot porte au maximum deux accents dynamiques, qui ont à peu près la même intensité'; with several heavy syllables each is stressed (e.g. [kɐˈsɐːˈlɐːt], [ˈkɐːpʊɲɐˈnɔːl]); with three heavy syllables the first and last are stressed and the middle one weakened; with two closed syllables both are stressed ([ˈcɛmˈmɛk], [kɐˈfɔŋkɔˈlɔŋ]); in all-light words of more than three syllables a second accent is heard on the penult, the syllable bearing the pitch peak ([ˈɛpʊlɐˈpʊlɐ] 'canard').
new_statements.exceptions: Authors hedge throughout ('Il semble qu’un mot porte au maximum deux accents', 'Les règles suivantes semblent diriger le système'); the archive cover sheet flags SIL Senegal e-publications as possibly preliminary working papers. §3.2.1.2 (p. 10): rare geminate-like long consonants are not distinctive and are 'peut-être associée à l’accent dynamique', left for later study. Words are mostly 1-4 syllables; 5-syllable words are compounds/reduplications and still show only two dynamic accents. No lexical exceptions or loanword behaviour discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly the 'mot phonologique' (§3.4), the same domain over which ATR vowel harmony spreads and never beyond; data are elicited citation forms from two main consultants (Paul Ekiyen Jaaju, of Hilol origin, raised in Darsilami, Gambia; Remy Alkali Sambu, of Kouba, living in Marakissa, Gambia). Phrase-level intonation is not treated here (Wilkinson & Berndt 2011 mention rising/falling intonation only for imperatives and polar questions).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 'le karone' / kulonay (speakers: kaloon, sg. aloon; 'Karoninka' in Gambia) = Glottolog karo1294 / ISO krx, no dialect subdivision made; consultants are islanders by origin (Hilol, Kouba) living in the Gambia (Darsilami/Fajikunda, Marakissa). SIL later spells the glossonym Kuloonaay. Same language as Sambou's 'joola karon'.

sources.note: §3.4.3 (doc pp. 15-17 = PDF pp. 17-19): no tone attested; 'hauteur musicale' (pitch) predictable, higher pitch on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word; 'accent dynamique' (intensity stress) predictable by syllable weight: heavy syllables (C)VV/(C)VVC/CVNC carry it, otherwise a closed (C)VC syllable, otherwise (all light) the first syllable; at most two dynamic accents per word, of about equal intensity; in all-light words of 4+ syllables a second accent is heard on the penult. §3.2.1.2 (p. 10): consonant length not distinctive, perhaps associated with dynamic accent.

EN gives consonant/vowel inventory only (citing Sambou 2002, Wilson 2007); FR gives alphabet (Jarju & Sagna 2016, SIL entry 76594) and cites 'Rosine Santos, Étude descriptive d'un dialecte diola : le karone (Sénégal). Phonologie, morphologie, syntaxe (?)'; neither mentions stress or tone.
